correctness.rationale: A uniform direction gives opposite signs for two facet normals with probability their angle divided by pi. There are exactly 2n cap edges with angle alpha and 2n belt edges with angle beta; direct cross products yield the two normal vectors and cosine formulas. The analytic derivative has a single sign change for all c=cos(pi/n) in [1/2,1). Solving its zero gives the unique positive minimizer; the equal-edge calculation is an exact algebraic identity. Seven-order symbolic/numeric tests, 675000 random directions and 2700 independent convex-hull reconstructions successfully replay the derived formulas.

value.rationale: The result supplies a nontrivial structural rigidity theorem for every right regular n-antiprism: the precise geometry of the uniquely optimal average silhouette coincides with equilateral lateral faces. This unifies all polygon orders, distinguishes flat and tall limiting silhouettes, gives a natural exact minimization statistic with a strict phase/sign change, and yields the universal large-order additive constant sqrt(3); it is not a mere single numerical evaluation.
